evaluations.label: A
errors: "Microphone placement unresolved: under flip ruled out" - the Project Manager argued for under the flip and then only said "the sides maybe is good"; nothing was formally ruled out.

"Weight intentional: users prefer something substantial in hand" - presents only the UI Designer's defense; the Industrial Designer said "you need to work on the weight a little bit", which the notes omit.
Next step "Align launch timing with a major sports event" has no owner and was a proposal the Project Manager agreed with in principle, not an assigned task.
"Web configurator" is an interpretation; the transcript only mentions pictures on the web and a rotating movie of the object.
strengths: Every number is right: EUR 12.50 budget, EUR 9.95 estimate, EUR 2-3 for the LCD, 8-9 million market, 2 million units = 25%, EUR 50 price, EUR 25 cost ceiling, EUR 25 profit per unit, 2-4 week evaluation.

Captures the button layout, the microphone argument (voice must work with the remote closed), the online drop-ship idea with Amazon/eBay, the Sony Pictures idea, and the no-redesign decision with second generation.
Concise, well structured, easy to scan; a reader gets the shape of the meeting quickly.
weaknesses: No names or roles anywhere, so the reader cannot tell who proposed what, who disagreed, or who committed to what.
Next steps carry no owners even though the Project Manager explicitly took on vendor negotiation and convincing management about Sony Pictures.
Omits that the production cost excludes advertising and transportation, the approval chain before real production (technical team, design team, management), and the EUR 1 case cost remark.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Action item owner "Christian" - no Christian in the meeting; the Industrial Designer is Christine, and no prototype-refinement task was assigned to anyone.

"Marketing Lead (Ed) - Develop and propose online sales and promotion strategy, including potential partnerships with Amazon/eBay and media companies like Sony Pictures" - never assigned; the online channel was the Industrial Designer's proposal and the Project Manager said he would convince management on Sony Pictures.
"Plan marketing campaigns aligning product launch with major sports events or DVD releases" assigned to Ed - not assigned in the meeting.
"Finalize detailed production budget including promotional and transport costs" - no one was asked to do this.
"Management - Approve current prototype design for market introduction without redesign" - the Project Manager already decided this in the meeting; it is not an open approval.
"Organize closing celebration event upon successful completion of production milestone" - the Project Manager proposed meeting that same evening for a party, not after a production milestone.
"Unknown (Finance Lead)" as owner of vendor negotiation - the Project Manager committed to it himself.
Summary says "voice control via side microphone" as a settled feature, while the body correctly says placement remains undecided.
"event-driven launches ... planned" - only proposed, not planned.

"team urged to monitor post-launch feedback closely" and "Emphasis on monitoring project outcomes after production and adjusting based on market response" - not said; the closing only said budget and evaluation results would come soon.
strengths: Most complete on content: the LCD exclusion from the cost sheet, the EUR 1 case cost, production cost excluding advertising and distribution, the circuit-board-vs-case scale point, the plasticine prototype, the 18-month market-change risk.
Correctly reports the core decision (no redesign before launch, feedback feeds a second generation) and the 2-4 week external prototype evaluation.
Keeps the microphone placement as undecided but leaning to the side, which matches the transcript.
weaknesses: The action-items section is largely invented: eleven items across six owners when the transcript contains two commitments, both by the Project Manager.
Wrong name (Christian) and vague owner labels (Unknown, Management, Technical/Product Team) make the action list misleading for anyone acting on it.
Verbose and repetitive; the "Leadership and Team Perspectives" section adds padding that was not discussed.

evaluations.label: C
errors: "IS1008d remote control prototype" - no product name is mentioned anywhere in the transcript.
"Agni presented the final design" - the presenter is Agnes (the Project Manager names "Christine and Agnes").
"Ed proposed shifting from traditional retail to an online 'drop ship' model" - the Industrial Designer (Christine) proposed it; the notes' own outline credits "Speaker 2".
"Ed suggested synchronizing the launch with major sporting events, such as the World Cup" - the Industrial Designer suggested the sync; Ed only named the World Cup as the peak season.

"Current calculations ... do not yet include advertising, transportation, or labor" - labor was in the cost (the EUR 1 case figure covered material and labor); the Marketing Expert excluded only advertising and transportation.

"Action Items (none)" - the Project Manager committed to negotiating with vendors and to convincing management about a Sony Pictures campaign; the outline itself says "Speaker 1 plans to negotiate with vendors".
Inconsistent speaker labels: the same person is "Agni" in the summary and "Speaker 4" in the outline; the Industrial Designer is "Christine" in one place and "Speaker 2" in another.
strengths: Numbers are right: EUR 9.95 vs EUR 12.50, EUR 2-3 for the LCD, 8-9 million market, 2 million units = 25%, EUR 50 price, 2-4 week evaluation.
Correctly records the no-further-changes decision and the UI Designer's concern about missing redesign time.
Captures the microphone debate with the right sides (Project Manager for under the flip; UI Designer and Marketing Expert for the side).
weaknesses: Two key proposals are misattributed to Ed, so a reader would credit the wrong person for the online channel and the sports-event launch.
Action items declared empty despite two explicit commitments in the transcript.
Summary and outline repeat each other with different speaker labels, and the Sony Pictures idea, the EUR 25 cost ceiling, and the approval chain before production are missing.

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Moritz" (used about seven times for the UI Designer) - no Moritz is in the transcript; the UI Designer is Agnes. The role attributions behind the name are all correct.
"Christine estimated the case could cost EUR 1 for material and labor" - the EUR 1 figure came from the Project Manager's cost sheet; Christine remarked that it was outstanding.
Owner labeled "Speaker 1" in the action items while the same person is "the company representative" in the body; neither is the transcript's role label (Project Manager).
strengths: Who said what is right throughout: Christine on circuit-board placement, weight, online drop-ship, market testing, sports-event sync and Sony Pictures; the UI Designer on closed-remote voice, egg-shaped buttons, redesign time and flop risk; the Project Manager on the no-redesign decision.
Both real commitments are listed with the correct owner and timestamp: vendor negotiation plus management cost talks, and convincing management on Sony Pictures.

Precise on numbers and nuance: independent study 8 million vs internal 8-9 million, EUR 25 cost ceiling leaving EUR 25 profit, end-of-January football games too soon, approval from technical team, other team and management before production.
Clearly shows the disagreement between the Project Manager (ship now) and the designers (test and allow time to respond).
weaknesses: A fabricated name for one participant is a real accuracy flaw and would confuse a reader who knows the team.
Less detail on the prototype itself (no button colors or layout) and Ed is never named, only "the marketing participant".
Omits the evening celebration and the disposable-diapers anecdote (minor).

rationale: D is the best record of what was decided and who will do what: every attribution by role is correct, both real commitments are listed with the right owner, and the disagreement over testing time is clear; its one flaw is calling the UI Designer "Moritz", a name that does not exist in the transcript. A is nearly error-free on numbers and content but names no one, so it cannot say who proposed, who objected or who owns a next step, and it slightly overstates the microphone and weight points. B has the fullest content but its action-items section is mostly invented (eleven items for six owners against two real commitments), it misnames Christine as Christian, and its summary states proposals as plans. C misattributes the online-channel and sports-event ideas to Ed, invents a product name, misspells Agnes, uses inconsistent speaker labels, and declares no action items when the Project Manager made two explicit commitments.
